LEGACY.Definition: something from the past that still affects things today

COME TO TERMS WITH.Definition: accept and learn to live with something difficult

IMPERIAL.Definition: relating to one country ruling over many other lands

LINGUA FRANCA.Definition: a language used between people whose first languages are different

VIRGIN.Definition: not yet explored, used or claimed by outsiders

SETTLEMENT.Definition: a place where people arrive to live and build homes

VENTURED.Definition: travelled somewhere new, accepting some risk

PLANTATIONS.Definition: large farms where crops such as sugar or cotton are grown

BRUSHED UNDER THE CARPET.Definition: hidden or ignored because it is embarrassing

CONVENIENTLY FORGOTTEN.Definition: ignored on purpose because remembering it is uncomfortable

INSEPARABLE.Definition: so closely joined that they cannot be divided

JEWEL IN THE CROWN.Definition: the most valuable or important part

OUTPOSTS.Definition: small bases set up far from the home country

OPIUM.Definition: a strong, addictive drug made from poppy plants

STRETCHING ITS MILITARY MUSCLES.Definition: using its army to show its strength

NORMS.Definition: usual or accepted ways of behaving

INSTITUTIONS.Definition: important organisations and systems in a society, such as courts and governments

BLANKET.Definition: covering every case in the same way

UPRISINGS.Definition: times when people fought against their rulers

HYPOCRITICAL.Definition: dishonest because its actions went against what it said

IMPLEMENTATION.Definition: setting up and putting into use

BUREAUCRATIC.Definition: run by officials following fixed rules

INFRASTRUCTURE.Definition: basic systems such as roads, railways and power supplies

BOOMING.Definition: growing quickly and doing very well

SCRATCHED THE SURFACE.Definition: dealt with a very small part of the subject
